headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: Airflow can egress broadly while Whisper is local-only audio processing, so the pair mainly risks unsafe handoff and workflow misuse rather than direct exfiltration.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Airflow has broad network egress, but Whisper has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or browser surfaces and no output-parsing interface is shown. The pairwise prompt-injection pathway is therefore not evidenced; uncertainty is low because both profiles lack a bridge.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Airflow output into Whisper prompts, then injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between them, then the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate queues.
Do not pipe Airflow text into Whisper prompts.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared workspace.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow can egress broadly, while Whisper is documented as local CLI-style audio processing with no network egress and no filesystem read/write. With no shared workspace or sensitive data class in either profile, direct leakage is not shown; the remaining risk is limited to unusual operator wiring.
conditions: IF Airflow is configured to pass sensitive text into Whisper inputs, then leakage risk increases.
IF a shared filesystem is introduced, then file-based leakage becomes plausible.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in Airflow task text.
Store Whisper inputs in a separate directory.
Review any outbound Airflow tasks for sensitive payloads.
Delete temporary audio files after processing.
requires-engineering: add DLP checks on Airflow egress.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surface is documented. Airflow has broad network egress but no filesystem write capability is listed; Whisper has no filesystem write, no git modification, and no subprocess or shell execution. Without a shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict becomes possible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, then coordination issues may appear.
mitigations: Keep outputs in separate directories.
Do not grant shared write permissions.
Run only one writer per resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate workflow outputs that a downstream system may treat as authoritative, and Whisper produces transcription text that can be consumed as input. The profiles do not show verification between them, so a bad transcription or bad orchestration decision could cascade into incorrect downstream actions. This is inferred from the pair, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Airflow consumes Whisper transcripts without validation, then errors can cascade.
IF downstream automation acts on those transcripts, then impact expands.
mitigations: Add a human review step for critical transcripts.
Validate transcript confidence before use.
Compare transcripts against source audio samples.
Log and flag low-confidence segments.
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. Airflow touches no data classes in the profile, and Whisper touches audio/speech only; there is no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or regulated data flow between them. The compliance pathway is therefore not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through both agents, compliance review is required.
IF retention policies diverge on shared audio, then a mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Document data retention for audio artifacts.
Review jurisdiction before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency.
